name: Vision & imaging
characteristic: Imaging regime: what sensing process produces the visual signal, and over what domain it is sampled (single frame, frames over time, 3D volume or surface, orbital sensor, clinical instrument, rendered page).
positive_test: The signal is a spatially sampled record of appearance or structure: pixels, voxels, frames or points.
negative_test: Rejects human or biological vision as the object of study (Vision Science, Visual Neuroscience -> Application > Neuroscience) and rejects rendering or plotting of results (Data Visualization, Computer Graphics).
notes: Branch-level surfaces sit here: Computer Vision 240+1, Visual Reasoning 3, Visual Representation Learning 2, Vision Transformers (translated per AXES.md 5). Branch total incl. children ~126 names / ~563 mentions. Per AXES.md 7's Bioinformatics ruling, generalised: `Computer Vision` names the branch, not a leaf.

name: Language & text
characteristic: Which variety of language the signal is, as language-technology communities divide their data: prose, interaction, program text, cross-lingual.
positive_test: The signal is a sequence of linguistic or symbolic tokens produced by a writer (or by a speaker and then transcribed).
negative_test: Rejects the acoustic waveform itself (-> Speech & audio), formal-language theory as machinery (-> Method), and `programming` in the mathematical-optimization sense.
notes: Branch-level surfaces sit here: Natural Language Processing 295+9, Language Modeling 12, Language Models 8, Large Language Models 5, Computational Linguistics 2. Branch total ~107 names / ~522 mentions.

name: Speech & audio
characteristic: What produces the acoustic signal: a voice, an instrument, or the environment.
positive_test: The signal is an acoustic waveform or a time-frequency representation of one.
negative_test: Rejects transcribed text (-> Language & text) and non-acoustic `signals` (physiological traces, graph signals).
notes: Branch-level surfaces: Audio Processing 3, Audio Signal Processing, Generative Models for Audio, Neural Audio Editing. Branch total ~25 names / ~46 mentions. Smallest substantive branch; kept because ASR/TTS/MIR are separate communities with separate venues.

name: Graphs & relational
characteristic: What the entities and the edges are - where the relation in the data comes from (asserted facts, observed interaction, relation that changes over time).
positive_test: The data's native form is a set of entities with explicit relations that the paper takes as given input.
negative_test: Rejects a graph used as a mathematical encoding of some other signal (molecular graphs, meshes, scene graphs, images-as-graphs); rejects graph theory and probabilistic graphical models as machinery (-> Method); rejects computer graphics and telecommunication networks (-> Application > Computing).
notes: Branch-level surfaces: Graph Neural Networks 76+4+1+1 (translated per AXES.md 5), Graph Learning 7, Graph Representation Learning 7, Node Classification 5, Graph Signal Processing 5. Branch total ~47 names / ~79 mentions plus the 82 GNN mentions that AXES.md 5 translates here. A translated architecture name lands on the branch node, never on a leaf: `Graph Neural Networks` does not say which kind of graph.

name: Time series & signals
characteristic: What physical or economic process generates the measurement stream (the body, an instrument, the environment, a market).
positive_test: The signal is one or more values measured repeatedly over time, and the temporal ordering is the research object.
negative_test: Rejects video and speech (their own branches); rejects sequence modeling as architecture (Sequence Modeling, Seq2Seq -> Method); rejects reinforcement-learning trajectories (no branch owns these - see RATIONALE D4).
notes: Branch-level surfaces: Time Series Forecasting 11, Time Series Analysis 8, Signal Processing 6, Temporal Point Processes 2, Probabilistic Forecasting 2. Branch total ~44 names / ~80 mentions.

name: Molecular & biological data
characteristic: Which physical entity the measurement describes: a small compound, a macromolecule, a genome, a cell population, or a solid.
positive_test: The signal describes matter or biological material - its structure, composition, dynamics or expression.
negative_test: Rejects the biological field served when the data is actually imagery or clinical records (Neuroimaging -> Vision; Epidemiology -> Application); rejects generic `sequence` names.
notes: Branch-level surfaces, per AXES.md 7's ruling that these name the whole branch: Bioinformatics 40, Computational Biology 33, Immunology 9, Systems Biology 3. Branch total ~111 names / ~306 mentions. Largest branch after vision and language.

name: Tabular & structured records
characteristic: Where the record comes from and what one row is (a sampled unit, a patient, a user-item event).
positive_test: The signal is a set of records with heterogeneous named fields, where no spatial, temporal or relational structure carries the meaning.
negative_test: Rejects a numeric matrix used only as a convenient optimizer benchmark; rejects database-systems research itself (-> Application > Computing).
notes: AXES.md 6 keeps this branch on 1 mention as a deliberate blind spot. Measured here it is not that empty once its children are populated: ~16 names / ~34 mentions, almost all via recommender-system and clinical-record surfaces. See RATIONALE D6 - the routing of `Recommender Systems` is a schema decision AXES.md never makes.

name: Multimodal
characteristic: Which cross-modal relationship a research community has actually formed around. Never an enumeration of pairs.
positive_test: The research question is about the relationship between modalities: alignment, fusion, cross-modal transfer or cross-modal retrieval.
negative_test: Rejects incidental co-occurrence: one optimizer tested on ImageNet and on WikiText gets {Vision, Text}, not Multimodal. Rejects a modality-agnostic method merely evaluated on two datasets.
notes: Branch-level surfaces: Multimodal Learning 15+3, Cross-Modal Learning, Multimodal Alignment, Multimodal Models, Multimodal Reasoning and Representation. Branch total ~26 names / ~60 mentions. `Multimodal Model Evaluation` is a contribution-type name -> mark_ignore (AXES.md 8b).

name: Uninformative
characteristic: Administrative row, not a branch (AXES.md 8b). Its two children divide by why the name carries no signal: a generic learning name vs a generic data name.
positive_test: The name is on-axis in phrasing (it is about data, or about learning from data) but names no kind of signal.
negative_test: Rejects names that are simply off-axis - method, architecture and task names are mark_ignore on this axis, not uninformative.
notes: Excluded from this axis's shares and reported as a line. ~27 names / ~552 mentions, i.e. the second-largest cluster on this axis after vision - almost all of it `Machine Learning` 249 and `Deep Learning` 177.

name: Natural imagery
positive_test: The signal is an ordinary photographic image of a scene or object, or an unqualified `image` with no instrument named.
negative_test: Rejects images produced by a clinical or orbital instrument; rejects frame sequences; rejects rendered charts and documents.
examples: Scene & object imagery; Fine-grained visual categories; Rendered & synthetic imagery
notes: Default reading for an unqualified image name: Image Classification 15, Object Detection 8, Image Segmentation 6, Semantic Segmentation 5. These are Task x Modality compounds that decompose exactly as AXES.md 4 says.

name: Video
positive_test: The signal is a sequence of frames and the paper uses its temporal structure.
negative_test: Rejects a single frame; rejects motion planning and motion capture that involve no image frames (those are control data, which this axis has no home for).
examples: Video understanding; Egocentric video; Tracking & motion sequences
notes: Video Prediction 3, Video Representation Learning 2, Video Generation/Retrieval/Processing/Interpolation/Synthesis/Perception/Learning, Object Tracking. Separated from natural imagery because video understanding is its own community, not because frames are a different tensor shape.

name: 3D geometry
positive_test: The signal is a 3D shape, surface or scene: point cloud, mesh, voxel grid, depth map or implicit field.
negative_test: Rejects `Geometric Deep Learning` 11 and 3D equivariance as method names (-> Method > Model design); rejects 3D atomic structures (-> Molecular); rejects 3D printing (-> Application).
examples: Point clouds; Meshes & surfaces; Neural scene representations
notes: 3D Modeling 3, 3D Reconstruction 2, 3D Shape Analysis 2, 3D Shape Generation 2, 3D Vision 2, Depth Estimation 2, Point Clouds, Neural Radiance Fields, SLAM. AXES.md 6 already names this child (~32 mentions); measured 38.

name: Biomedical imagery
positive_test: The image is produced by a clinical or laboratory instrument: MRI, CT, ultrasound, X-ray, microscope, histology slide, retinal camera.
negative_test: Rejects EEG and MEG traces, which are time series despite being called neuroimaging (-> Time series > Physiological signals); rejects the medical field served, which is a separate Application value.
examples: Radiological imaging (MRI/CT); Microscopy & histopathology; Retinal & dermatological imaging
notes: Medical Imaging 48, Neuroimaging 28, Medical Image Analysis 10, Medical Image Segmentation 8, fMRI variants 10, Microscopy 3+2+1, Ultrasound 3, Radiology 2. Always dual-mapped: AXES.md 7 pairs it with Application > Health or Neuroscience. Second-largest depth-2 node on this axis.

name: Remote-sensing imagery
positive_test: The image is captured from orbit or from the air, over a geographic area.
negative_test: Rejects `sensing` in the sense of a sensor time series (Tactile Sensing, Passive Sensing Technologies); rejects satellite communication (-> Application > Computing).
examples: Satellite imagery; Aerial & drone imagery; Hyperspectral imagery
notes: Remote Sensing 11+1, Geographical Information Systems 1. AXES.md 7 pairs it with Application > Physical & environmental sciences. Homonym note: 12 of the 16 papers whose name contains sensing/sensor are Remote Sensing, i.e. imagery, not sensor streams.

name: Document imagery
positive_test: The signal is a rendered page or figure whose content is symbolic: scanned text, forms, tables, charts, handwriting.
negative_test: Rejects digital text that was never rendered (-> Language & text > Written text); rejects software documentation (-> Application > Computing).
examples: Scanned documents; Charts & figures; Handwriting
notes: BLIND SPOT, kept deliberately (AXES.md 9, same policy as Tabular). Only Chart Understanding 1 and Document Classification 1. Document AI / OCR is a large, venue-bearing area of the field that this single institute-year barely contains; a 2023-2026 re-extraction will populate it.

name: Written text
positive_test: The signal is written prose or documents: articles, posts, reviews, papers, records written in natural language.
negative_test: Rejects multi-turn interaction (-> Conversational language), program text (-> Source code), and the cross-lingual data regime (-> Multilingual text).
examples: Web & news text; Social media text; Scientific & clinical text
notes: Question Answering 14, Text Classification 8, Sentiment Analysis 6, Prompt Engineering 6, Named Entity Recognition 5, Text Generation 5, Social Media Analysis 3, Misinformation Detection 3, Summarization 3+2+1. Most of these are Task x Modality compounds that decompose. Social-media text (~10 mentions) is listed as a depth-3 rather than a depth-2: it is a register of written text, not a different signal.

name: Conversational language
positive_test: The signal is multi-turn interaction between participants, where the turn structure matters.
negative_test: Rejects single-turn prompting of a model; rejects speech audio of a conversation (-> Speech & audio).
examples: Task-oriented dialogue; Open-domain conversation; Human-agent interaction transcripts
notes: Dialogue Systems 7, Conversational AI 4+1, Dialog Systems 1, Pragmatics in Language Understanding 1.

name: Source code
positive_test: The signal is program text or another formal notation that a machine executes or checks.
negative_test: Rejects software engineering as a field served (-> Application > Computing, AXES.md 7 amendment); rejects `programming` in the mathematical-optimization sense - 12 of the 16 corpus names containing `programming` are integer/stochastic/dynamic programming.
examples: Source-code corpora; Formal specifications & proofs; Structured query languages
notes: Code Generation 7, Program Synthesis 3, Code Completion/Search/Summarization/Synthesis, Automated Program Repair, Text-to-SQL, Source Code Analysis, Static Code Analysis. AXES.md 6 does not mention code anywhere; placed here by judgement because code LLM work is continuous with text LLM work (see RATIONALE).

name: Multilingual text
positive_test: The research object is text in more than one language, or in a language with little data.
negative_test: Rejects multimodal `translation` (Image-to-Image Translation); rejects multilingual code (that is Source code with a multilingual note).
examples: Parallel corpora; Low-resource languages; Cross-lingual transfer corpora
notes: Machine Translation 15, Cross-lingual Transfer Learning 3, Multilingual NLP 2, Multilingual Models 2, Low-Resource Languages 1. AXES.md 6 lists `machine translation 15` as a child of Language & text, but MT is a Task under AXES.md 4; what MT contributes to *this* axis is the multilingual data regime, which is what this node names.

name: Speech
positive_test: The acoustic signal is a human voice carrying language or speaker identity.
negative_test: Rejects the transcript (-> Language & text); rejects singing voice used as music (-> Music).
examples: Read & spontaneous speech; Speaker & voice data; Pathological & clinical speech
notes: Speech Recognition 7, Speech Processing 6, ASR 3+1, Speech Enhancement 2, Speech Separation 2, Speaker Verification 2+1, Speech Synthesis, Speaker Embedding, Speech Emotion Recognition.

name: Music
positive_test: The signal is music, as audio or as a symbolic score.
negative_test: Rejects recommendation machinery (Music Recommendation is Task > Recommendation with this modality); rejects general audio events.
examples: Symbolic music scores; Music audio recordings; Multi-track stems
notes: Music Generation 2, Automatic Music Transcription 1, Music Information Retrieval 1, Music Source Separation 1, Music Recommendation Systems 1.

name: Environmental sound
positive_test: The signal is non-speech, non-music sound: acoustic scenes, events, animal calls, machine noise.
negative_test: Rejects speech and music; rejects ultrasound imaging, which is an image, not a sound recording.
examples: Acoustic scenes & events; Bioacoustic recordings; Industrial & machine sound
notes: Audio Classification 3, Sound Recognition 1, Bioacoustic AI 1. Thin but the community (DCASE, bioacoustics) is real; kept as a near-blind-spot.

name: Knowledge graphs
positive_test: Edges are asserted facts with named relation types, curated into a base.
negative_test: Rejects an embedding method that happens to be evaluated on a KG; rejects knowledge representation as a theory topic (-> Method).
examples: Entity-relation knowledge bases; Biomedical knowledge graphs; Ontologies & taxonomies
notes: Knowledge Graph Reasoning 2, Knowledge Graphs 1, Inductive Knowledge Graph Reasoning 1, Biological Knowledge Graphs 1 (Knowledge Base Question Answering 1 dual-maps with Written text).

name: Social & information networks
positive_test: Edges are observed interactions or references between real entities: people, documents, species, genes.
negative_test: Rejects telecommunication and transport infrastructure networks (-> Application > Computing / Industry); rejects neural networks in every sense.
examples: Social interaction networks; Citation & information networks; Biological interaction networks
notes: Network Science 1, Network Analysis 1, Causal Inference in Social Networks 1, Information Diffusion 1, Ecological Network Prediction 1, Multi-Relational Data Modeling 1, plus Gene Regulatory Networks 2 which dual-map with Molecular. Compound name retained: `Social and Information Networks` is the field's own name for one thing (arXiv cs.SI).

name: Temporal graphs
positive_test: The relations themselves change over time and the change is the research object.
negative_test: Rejects a static graph with time-stamped node features; rejects time series on a fixed graph (that is a graph signal, which stays at branch level).
examples: Dynamic interaction graphs; Streaming graph updates; Temporal knowledge graphs
notes: Dynamic Graphs 3, Temporal Graphs 2, Dynamic Graph Representation Learning 1, Temporal Graph Learning 1, Graph Dynamics 1, Dynamic Link Prediction 1, Temporal Network Models 1. This sibling is divided by edge dynamics rather than edge provenance - the one place this sibling set strains its characteristic (see RATIONALE).

name: Physiological signals
positive_test: The measurement stream comes from a living body: brain, heart, muscle, movement, sleep.
negative_test: Rejects anatomical or functional *images* of the same organ (fMRI volumes -> Vision > Biomedical imagery); rejects the clinical field served (-> Application > Health).
examples: EEG & MEG recordings; Neural spike recordings; Cardiac & wearable vital signs
notes: Brain-Computer Interfaces 3+2, Electrophysiology 3, Brain-Machine Interfaces 2, Biomedical Signal Processing 2, EEG Analysis, EEG Decoding, Medical Signal Processing, Clinical Time Series Modeling, MEG 1+1, Clinical Neurophysiology, Sleep Research. AXES.md 6 names this child; the EEG/fMRI boundary it leaves unstated is fixed by the negative test above.

name: Sensor streams
positive_test: The measurement stream comes from an instrument or a device: inertial units, tactile sensors, spectrometers, GPS traces.
negative_test: Rejects remote sensing, which is imagery; rejects sensory systems as neuroscience (-> Application); rejects robot control signals (this axis has no home for those).
examples: Inertial & motion sensors; Tactile signals; Spectrometry & instrument traces
notes: Tactile Sensing, Haptics and Tactile Interaction, Sensor Fusion (dual-maps to Multimodal), Passive Sensing Technologies, Mass Spectrometry, Trajectory Prediction, Pedestrian Inertial Navigation, Spatio-temporal Analysis. Thin; also the natural home for mobility/trajectory data, which the corpus barely contains.

name: Environmental time series
positive_test: The measurement stream comes from the physical environment: climate, weather, seismic, hydrological, astronomical.
negative_test: Rejects climate governance and climate policy (-> Application / Desired properties); rejects satellite images of the environment (-> Vision > Remote-sensing imagery).
examples: Climate & weather series; Seismic & geophysical traces; Astronomical light curves
notes: Environmental Monitoring 4, Climate Model Emulation 2, Climate Data Downscaling 1, Climate Data Preprocessing 1, Climate and Weather Modelling 1, Renewable Energy Forecasting 1. Gridded climate fields are spatiotemporal, not scalar series; that is a depth-3 distinction, not a reason to split the node.

name: Financial time series
positive_test: The measurement stream is an economic quantity observed over time: prices, demand, load, indicators.
negative_test: Rejects finance and economics as fields served (-> Application > Industry & commerce / Social sciences); rejects game-theoretic market models (-> Method).
examples: Asset-price series; Demand & load series; Macroeconomic indicators
notes: BLIND SPOT, kept deliberately. Only Econometrics 1, Energy Market Modeling 1, auction-data simulation 1, and none of the three is unambiguously this node. Financial/operational forecasting is a large area of the field with essentially no presence in this institute-year; a node is kept so a re-extraction has somewhere to land.

name: Small molecules
positive_test: The entity is a chemical compound: a drug candidate, a ligand, a reagent, a reaction.
negative_test: Rejects materials and crystals (-> Materials); rejects biological macromolecules (-> Proteins); rejects chemistry as a field served when the data is imagery or text.
examples: Molecular graphs & SMILES; Conformers & 3D structures; Reaction data
notes: Computational Chemistry 12, Drug Discovery 7, Molecular Property Prediction 7+1, Molecular Biology 5, Molecular Machine Learning 4, Quantum Chemistry 4, Molecular Dynamics 3+1, Molecule Generation 2, Molecular Design 2, Cheminformatics/Chemoinformatics 4. `Molecular Graphs` maps here, not to Graphs: a graph is the encoding, the molecule is the signal.

name: Proteins
positive_test: The entity is a protein or another biological macromolecule: its structure, its sequence, its binding or dynamics.
negative_test: Rejects protein-coding genomic sequence studies (-> Genomic sequences); rejects `Protein Language Models` as an architecture claim - it maps here because the signal is a protein.
examples: Protein structures; Protein sequences; Protein-ligand complexes
notes: Protein Structure Prediction 5, Structural Biology 4, Protein Function Prediction 3, Protein Representation Learning 3, Protein Dynamics, Protein-Ligand Binding, Protein-Protein Interaction Prediction, Protein Structure Modeling, RNA Design. TAIL_VALIDATION already validates `Protein Structure Prediction` and `Protein Language Models` reaching this branch.

name: Genomic sequences
positive_test: The signal is nucleic-acid sequence or variation data: DNA, RNA, variants, phylogeny.
negative_test: Rejects generic sequence modeling - measured, 17 of the 26 papers whose name contains `sequen` are Sequence Modeling / Seq2Seq / Sequential Learning, which are Method names. Rejects expression matrices (-> Omics profiles).
examples: DNA sequence data; RNA sequences; Variant & population-genetic data
notes: Genomics 26, Genetics 10, Phylogenetics 4, Proteogenomics 2, Biological Sequence Design 2, Multiple Sequence Alignment, Bulk Sequencing, Population/Cancer/Microbial/Viral/Regulatory Genomics. Always dual-mapped with Application > Life sciences. This is the node AXES.md 6 calls `sequences`, renamed: see RATIONALE D2.

name: Omics profiles
positive_test: The signal is a measured abundance matrix over cells or samples: transcriptome, proteome, metabolome.
negative_test: Rejects the sequencing *protocol* when the research object is the genome itself (-> Genomic sequences); rejects multi-omics *integration*, which is a relationship between modalities (-> Multimodal).
examples: Single-cell RNA-seq; Bulk transcriptomics; Proteomic & metabolomic profiles
notes: Proteomics 6, Single-cell Analysis 3, Single-Cell Genomics 2, Single-cell Sequencing 2, Transcriptomics 2, Single-Cell Transcriptomics, Clinical Proteomics, Cancer Transcriptomics, single-cell RNA-seq analysis/simulation. Split from Genomic sequences on judgement: an expression matrix is not a sequence and the single-cell community is separate.

name: Materials
positive_test: The entity is a solid or bulk material: a crystal, an alloy, a device material, an atomistic system.
negative_test: Rejects material *science as a field served* when the paper's data is imagery; rejects molecular dynamics of biomolecules (-> Proteins / Small molecules).
examples: Crystal structures; Atomistic simulation trajectories; Spectral material properties
notes: Material Science 3, Materials Science 3, Materials Modeling 2, Materials Discovery, Crystallography, ML for Materials Discovery/Science, 3D Atomic Systems, Molecular and material modeling. AXES.md 6 names this child. Sits under a branch called `Molecular & biological` although a crystal is neither molecular nor biological - the branch's real characteristic is `matter`, see RATIONALE.

name: Tabular feature data
positive_test: The signal is a table of rows and heterogeneous named columns, mixing categorical and numeric fields, with no other structure.
negative_test: Rejects a homogeneous numeric matrix used as an optimizer benchmark; rejects feature engineering as a method topic.
examples: Heterogeneous feature tables; Mixed categorical-numeric data; Missing & imputed data
notes: BLIND SPOT, kept per AXES.md 6's explicit ruling. Categorical Data 2, Data Imputation 1, Imputation 1, Database Systems 1. Tabular deep learning (TabPFN, GBDT-vs-NN) is an active area with no presence here.

name: Electronic health records
positive_test: The signal is a structured longitudinal record about a person held by an institution: encounters, codes, labs, registry entries.
negative_test: Rejects clinical *text* notes (-> Language & text > Written text); rejects medical images (-> Vision); rejects epidemiology as a field served (-> Application > Health).
examples: Longitudinal patient records; Disease registries; Administrative claims
notes: BLIND SPOT, mostly. Healthcare Analytics 2, Clinical Data Analysis 1, Clinical datasets 1, Patient Data Management 1, Rare Disease Registries 1. Epidemiology 20 and Public Health 12 almost certainly ride on record data but name only their field, so the modality is invisible to the extraction.

name: User interaction records
positive_test: The signal is a log of interactions between users and items or a system: ratings, clicks, purchases, sessions.
negative_test: Rejects recommendation as an output specification, which is Task > Recommendation (AXES.md 7); this node records only what the data is.
examples: User-item interaction logs; Clickstream & session logs; Transaction records
notes: Recommender Systems 16, Recommendation Systems 3, Cultural Content Recommendation 2, Movie Recommendation 1, Fairness in Recommender Systems 1, plus Music Recommendation Systems. JUDGEMENT, flagged: AXES.md routes `Recommender Systems` to Task and never says what its modality is. Mapping it here is what lifts this branch off 1 mention; the conservative alternative is to leave it modality-silent, which returns the branch to blind-spot status.

name: Vision-language
positive_test: The research question concerns the correspondence between images or video and text: alignment, grounding, captioning, text-to-image generation, cross-modal retrieval.
negative_test: Rejects a vision model that happens to use a text-derived label space; rejects text-only evaluation of a multimodal model (that is a Task/contribution question).
examples: Image-text pairs; Video-language; Vision-language-action
notes: Vision-Language Models 11, Visual Question Answering 4+1, Vision-and-Language 3+1+1, Vision-Language Pretraining 2, Text-to-Image 4 names, Image Captioning, Vision-Language Alignment, Vision-Language Compositionality. The only multimodal child with substantial corpus support, matching AXES.md 6's ~26.

name: Audio-visual
positive_test: The research question concerns the correspondence between sound and image: audio-visual speech, sound localisation in video, cross-modal generation.
negative_test: Rejects video with a text transcript (that is vision-language); rejects speech alone.
examples: Audio-visual speech; Sound source localization; Audio-visual event data
notes: BLIND SPOT, kept. Measured: zero corpus names contain `audio-visual` or `lip`. AXES.md 6 asserts this child with no corpus support; the community exists (AVSR, AVE) so it is kept under AXES.md 9's speculative-but-justified rule, and flagged as such rather than silently carried.

name: Multimodal biomedical data
positive_test: The research question concerns integrating heterogeneous biomedical measurements of the same subject: imaging with omics, imaging with records, multi-omics.
negative_test: Rejects a single biomedical modality; rejects multi-centre or multi-site data, which is a distribution-shift question (-> Method).
examples: Imaging-genetics; Multi-omics integration; Imaging plus clinical records
notes: Multi-Omics 1, Single-Cell Multi-Omics 1, Imaging Transcriptomics 1, Genomics and Metabolomics 1, Electrophysiology and Neuroimaging 1. Five distinct single-paper names in one year is the signature of a real community under-named by the extraction. AXES.md 6 lists `multimodal medical` as a child; confirmed.

name: Sensor fusion
positive_test: The research question concerns combining heterogeneous sensing streams into one percept: camera with lidar, radar, depth or proprioception.
negative_test: Rejects fusing two feature extractors over the same modality; rejects multi-view imagery from identical cameras.
examples: Camera-lidar fusion; Radar-camera fusion; Proprioception-vision fusion
notes: BLIND SPOT, kept. Only Sensor Fusion 1. The autonomous-driving and robot-perception communities are large; their near-absence here is a property of this institute-year (robotics work is present but named by its application, not its sensors).

name: Modality-unspecified learning
positive_test: The name denotes learning or intelligence in general and names no signal at all.
negative_test: Rejects names that denote a method aspect (Self-Supervised Learning, Optimization) - those are informative on the Method axis and simply absent from this one.
examples: (none - administrative)
notes: Machine Learning 249+1, Deep Learning 177+56 mentions, Artificial Intelligence 15, Neural Networks 19, Artificial Neural Networks 4. AXES.md 5's third row routes exactly these here on every axis. Reported as a line, excluded from shares.

name: Generic data names
positive_test: The name is about data as such - its quality, quantity, provenance or curation - without naming a kind of signal.
negative_test: Rejects data curation as a *method* topic (Data Augmentation, Active Learning -> Method > Data curation); this node is only for names with no method content either.
examples: (none - administrative)
notes: Data Analysis 4, Dataset Creation 3, Predictive Modeling 3, Data Curation 2, Data Mining 2, Big Data Analysis/Analytics, Synthetic Data, Data Quality, Dataset Bias. Answers TAIL_VALIDATION F5 for this axis.
